done_when: forge doctor --fix finds changed-by-hand files with one git status and one git log call for all of Forge's files instead of two calls per file, with the same results; a command test counts git calls per doctor --fix run and shows they no longer grow with the number of files; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

findings.body: If N Forge files were edited by hand in N separate commits already landed on the default branch, this loop calls `_held` once per commit. Each call evaluates `pin(commit)` and `pin(commit^)`, and `src/forge/story.py:605` implements each lookup with a separate `git show` process. Consequently, both default-branch runs and fix-branch runs containing those landed commits still add 2N git calls, violating the required fixed total as changed files grow. The performance test's two adoption cases miss this: tests/test_doctor_batches_file_checks.py:73–77 commit all changed paths together on an unlanded fix branch, bypassing these pin lookups entirely. Batch the pin checks too, and cover separately landed edits with the command-level call counter.
findings.title: Not done: doctor --fix git-call count still grows with separately landed hand edits

why: forge doctor --fix checks every Forge file with two git commands each (about 190 git processes per run)
